title: Top 10 Cloud Computing Services for Indian Businesses (2026)
excerpt: A use-case-led guide to ten cloud services an Indian business may consider, from Azure and AWS to Microsoft 365, Zoho and backup, with a comparison table and how to choose.
body:
This is a use-case-led list, not a measured ranking. We have not benchmarked these services, and no analyst or survey places them in this order. The ten entries are grouped by the job they do for an Indian business: infrastructure platforms where you run servers and databases, productivity suites where your staff work every day, business applications, and the storage and backup layer that protects the rest. Pick by the job you need done, then compare two or three candidates on cost, support and compliance.

A note on scope. TechZoid Technologies supplies Microsoft Azure consumption, Microsoft 365, Zoho and Adobe and Autodesk licences, and provides Azure, cloud, backup and Microsoft 365 services. We do not list AWS or Google Cloud as products; where they appear below, we advise on them and say so. That is a fact about our catalogue, not a verdict on the platforms.

## The ten at a glance

| # | Service | Main job | Typical buyer | Billing model |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Microsoft Azure | General cloud platform, strong with Windows and Microsoft workloads | Mid-size and large firms already on Microsoft | Pay-as-you-go or committed consumption |
| 2 | Amazon Web Services (AWS) | Broadest general cloud platform | Start-ups, product companies, large enterprises | Pay-as-you-go, commitments available |
| 3 | Google Cloud | Data, analytics and containers | Data-heavy and engineering-led teams | Pay-as-you-go, commitments available |
| 4 | Oracle Cloud Infrastructure | Oracle database and Oracle application workloads | Firms running Oracle estates | Pay-as-you-go, commitments available |
| 5 | Microsoft 365 | Email, Office apps, Teams, device security | Almost every office-based business | Per user, monthly or annual |
| 6 | Google Workspace | Email, Docs, Meet, Drive | Browser-first teams | Per user |
| 7 | Zoho | CRM, accounting, helpdesk and mail from one publisher | SMEs wanting integrated business apps | Per user per app, or bundled |
| 8 | OneDrive for Business and SharePoint | File storage and sharing | Teams on Microsoft 365 | Per user |
| 9 | Cloud backup and recovery | Offsite copies and disaster recovery | Every business holding data worth keeping | Per workload or per terabyte |
| 10 | Salesforce | CRM-led customer platform | Sales-led mid-size and large firms | Per user, by edition |

## Infrastructure platforms: where servers and databases run

### 1. Microsoft Azure

Azure is the natural cloud for businesses whose servers, identity and desktops already run on Microsoft. It works with Windows Server, SQL Server and Active Directory-style identity, and you may be able to carry existing licences across using Microsoft's licence-mobility and hybrid benefits, which we check against your actual agreements. Microsoft operates Azure regions in India, so data can be kept in the country where your policy requires it.

TechZoid sells [Azure consumption](/products/azure-consumption-commitment) as a commitment against which your usage is billed, invoiced in India with GST. Pricing is confirmed on a written quotation through [an enquiry](/enquiry). We also provide [Azure services](/services/azure), from landing-zone design to migration and ongoing cost review. Azure suits you when identity, email and file services are Microsoft already and you want one invoice and one support relationship.

### 2. Amazon Web Services

AWS is the widest general-purpose cloud, with a very large catalogue of services and a deep pool of engineers in India who know it. That talent pool is a practical advantage: hiring or contracting for AWS skills is usually easier than for niche platforms. It is common among start-ups and product companies and also among large enterprises. TechZoid does not list AWS as a product; we advise on architecture and cost, and our [AWS advisory page](/services/aws) explains how. Its breadth is also its trap: the number of options makes cost control a skill in itself.

### 3. Google Cloud

Google Cloud is often chosen for analytics, data warehousing, machine-learning work and containerised applications. Teams that already use Google Workspace sometimes prefer to keep identity and billing relationships in one family. As with AWS, TechZoid does not list Google Cloud as a product and offers [advisory help](/services/google-cloud) rather than resale. Check which Indian regions host the specific services you need, since not every service is available in every region.

### 4. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure

Oracle Cloud Infrastructure is the sensible place to look if your core systems are Oracle databases or Oracle business applications, because licensing, support and tuning can be discussed in one conversation. For firms without an Oracle estate it is rarely the first pick. Oracle's licensing rules are particular, so read the terms for bringing existing licences before you assume a saving. Our Oracle brand page lists what we can quote.

## Productivity and collaboration: where staff work

### 5. Microsoft 365

For most Indian offices this is the first cloud service they buy, whether they call it that or not. It bundles business email, the Office apps, Teams, OneDrive storage and, in the higher plans, device management and security controls. Choosing between plans is a security and management question as much as a feature one: our guide to [Business Standard versus Business Premium](/blog/microsoft-365-business-standard-vs-business-premium) walks through it, and [Business Premium](/products/microsoft-365-business-premium) is the plan to look at when you want managed devices and stronger protection. Licences are invoiced in INR with GST, and we also provide [Microsoft 365 services](/services/microsoft-365) for migration and tenant setup. The wider range is on our [Microsoft 365 page](/microsoft-365).

### 6. Google Workspace

Google Workspace gives you email, documents, video meetings and shared drives, all browser-first. Teams that live in a browser and collaborate on shared documents often like it. Large offline spreadsheet models, heavy Excel macros and specialist desktop add-ins are where firms usually hit friction. We compare the two in [Microsoft 365 versus Google Workspace for Indian SMEs](/blog/microsoft-365-versus-google-workspace-for-indian-smes). The honest rule is to follow your existing file formats and the tools your clients send you.

### 7. Zoho

Zoho is an Indian-headquartered publisher with a broad range of business applications, including [CRM](/products/zoho-crm), [Books](/products/zoho-books), [Desk](/products/zoho-desk) and [Mail](/products/zoho-mail), plus [Zoho One](/products/zoho-one), a bundle of its applications. It is attractive for SMEs that want sales, accounts and support in one consistent family without assembling five separate tools. Test the accounting features against your own GST filing process, and confirm which data-centre locations your plan uses. See also our [Zoho brand page](/brands/zoho).

### 8. OneDrive for Business and SharePoint

If your problem is shared files rather than a whole suite, cloud file storage is the focused answer. [OneDrive for Business](/products/onedrive-for-business-plan-1) stores each person's files with sharing controls, and SharePoint serves team sites. This is also useful for retiring an ageing office file server. Remember that sync is not backup: deleted or overwritten files can propagate. That leads to the next entry.

## Business applications and protection

### 9. Cloud backup and recovery

Backup is the cloud service people forget until the day they need it. A sensible design keeps at least one copy off the primary system, separated from the credentials an attacker would use, and tests restoring. Software such as Veeam and [Acronis](/brands/acronis) can send copies to cloud storage, and you can also use cloud-native tools from the platforms above. Our [backup and disaster recovery service](/services/backup-disaster-recovery) designs this around the recovery time and recovery point you can afford, and our [backup software category](/backup-software) shows what we can quote. Do not skip the written restore test.

### 10. Salesforce

Salesforce is a customer relationship platform aimed at sales-led organisations that want extensive customisation and a large ecosystem of implementation partners. It tends to need a project, administrators and a budget for configuration, so it is more typical of mid-size and larger firms. Smaller businesses often find Zoho or Microsoft's own offerings simpler to adopt. Our Salesforce brand page lists what we can quote on enquiry.

## India-specific points to check for any of the ten

**Data residency.** Several providers operate regions inside India. Confirm the exact region for each service you will use, because a provider can offer a region for compute and still keep a given feature elsewhere. Write the region into your contract or order form rather than relying on a brochure.

**The DPDP Act and sector rules.** India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 places duties on organisations that process personal data, and sector regulators add their own expectations. Banks, insurers, payment firms, listed companies and government bodies often face specific outsourcing, audit or localisation requirements. We are not your lawyer. Ask your compliance team what applies, then ask each provider for its written commitments on location, breach notification, sub-processors and exit.

**INR billing and GST.** Many Indian buyers prefer to be invoiced in rupees by an Indian entity with GST shown, because it simplifies accounting and input credit. GST on cloud and software services is generally claimable by GST-registered businesses, which is why a tax invoice matters. Read our note on [GST input credit on software purchases](/blog/gst-input-credit-on-software-purchases). Foreign-currency billing on a card exposes you to exchange-rate swings and card limits.

**Support and partners.** Ask who answers the phone at 11 pm, in which language, and under what service level. Partners in India often provide the first line of help, billing and local advice, with the publisher behind them. A partner that also does the architecture work can save you from a design that is expensive to run.

**Cost control.** Cloud bills grow quietly. Set budgets and alerts from day one, tag resources by team, switch off development systems outside working hours, and review commitments yearly. Our guide on [planning a cloud migration that does not cost more](/blog/planning-a-cloud-migration-that-does-not-cost-more) covers the traps.

## How to choose

1. **Start from the workload, not the brand.** List what you want to run: email, files, a line-of-business application, a website, a database, analytics, backups.
2. **Follow your existing estate.** Microsoft servers and identity point to Azure and Microsoft 365. Oracle databases point to Oracle. A browser-first culture points to Google.
3. **Count the skills you have.** A platform your engineers do not know costs more than any discount saves.
4. **Compare total cost, not list rates.** Include data transfer, support, backup, licences you must still pay for, and the staff time to manage it.
5. **Check compliance early.** Settle region, audit rights and exit terms before you migrate, not after.
6. **Keep an exit.** Know how you would take your data and applications back out, and how long it would take.
7. **Pilot small.** Move one low-risk workload first and review the first three bills.

Many Indian businesses end up with a mix: Microsoft 365 or Zoho for people, one infrastructure platform for servers, and independent backup. That is normal, and it is easier to manage when one partner handles the invoices and the first line of support.

## Where TechZoid fits

Tell us the workloads and the number of users through [an enquiry](/enquiry), and we will suggest a shortlist and confirm pricing on a written quotation. Website prices are tentative; the quotation fixes the price.

faqs.question: Is this a ranking of the best cloud providers in India?
faqs.answer: No. It is a use-case-led list of ten services an Indian business may consider, grouped by the job they do. We have not benchmarked them, and the order is not a measurement of quality. Choose by workload, existing systems, skills and compliance needs.

faqs.question: Does TechZoid sell AWS or Google Cloud?
faqs.answer: No. We do not list AWS or Google Cloud as products. We advise on them, including architecture and cost review. What we do sell is Microsoft Azure consumption, Microsoft 365, and Zoho, Adobe and Autodesk licences, with Azure, cloud, backup and Microsoft 365 services alongside.

faqs.question: Do I need to keep my data in India?
faqs.answer: It depends on your sector and contracts. The DPDP Act, 2023 and sector regulators set expectations, and some regulated firms and government bodies have stricter rules. Ask your compliance team, then get the region and exit terms written into the order form.

faqs.question: Can I get a GST invoice for cloud services?
faqs.answer: Where you buy through an Indian entity, you can receive a GST invoice, and GST is usually claimable as input credit by GST-registered buyers. Confirm the invoicing entity before you order. Foreign-currency card billing generally does not give you the same paperwork.

faqs.question: Is cloud file sync the same as backup?
faqs.answer: No. Sync services mirror changes, so a deletion or ransomware encryption can spread to every copy. A backup keeps separate, restorable versions, ideally off the primary system and with different credentials. Test a restore before you rely on it.

faqs.question: How do I control cloud costs after migrating?
faqs.answer: Set budgets and alerts, tag resources by team, shut down non-production systems out of hours, and review commitments yearly. Compare the first three bills with the estimate. Our Azure service includes cost review, and we can advise on other platforms too.
